R. 3276 _______________________________________________________________________ AN ACT To direct the Secretary of the Interior to establish the Urban Bird Treaty Program. Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives of the United States of America in Congress assembled, SECTION 1. SHORT TITLE. This Act may be cited as the ``Local Communities & Bird Habitat Stewardship Act of 2026''. SEC. 2. URBAN BIRD TREATY PROGRAM. (a) Urban Bird Treaty Program.-- (1) In general.--The Director shall establish a program for the voluntary conservation of birds and the habitats of such birds in urban areas, to be known as the ``Urban Bird Treaty Program''. (2) Program duties.--In carrying out the Program, the Director shall-- (A) work with and support covered entities to-- (i) protect, restore, or enhance urban habitats for birds, including through the control of invasive species and restoration of native plant species; (ii) reduce urban hazards to birds; (iii) engage communities in scientific activities involving the monitoring of birds and the habitats of such birds in urban areas; and (iv) educate and engage communities in caring about and conserving birds and the habitats of such birds in urban areas; (B) provide technical and financial assistance through partnerships with covered entities to build capacity for, plan, and carry out projects related to activities described in subparagraph (A); and (C) facilitate collaboration and information sharing among covered entities and the public with respect to best management practices for the conservation, restoration, and enhancement of urban bird habitats. (3) Grant program.-- (A) In general.--The Director shall establish a competitive grant program to award amounts to eligible entities for the purposes of conducting research, planning, assessments, management, building capacity, monitoring, collaboration and information sharing, workforce training, and accomplishing related activities as described in paragraph (2) with respect to the conservation, restoration, enhancement or management of urban birds and the habitats of urban birds. (B) Applications.--To be eligible for a grant under this paragraph, an eligible entity shall submit to the Director an application in such form, at such time, and containing such information as the Director determines appropriate. (C) Administration.-- (i) Agreement.--The Director may enter into an agreement with the Foundation for the Foundation to administer the grant program established under subparagraph (A) pursuant to the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation Establishment Act (16 U.S.C. 3701 et seq.). (ii) Application of national fish and wildlife foundation establishment act.--Section 10(a) of the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation Establishment Act (16 U.S.C. 3709(a)) shall not apply with respect to-- (I) an agreement entered into under clause (i); or (II) amounts made available to carry out this section. (iii) Geographic distribution.--The Director shall ensure, to the extent practicable, equitable distribution of awards among and between small, midsize, and large cities, as described in the document titled ``Education Demographic and Geographic Estimates Program (EDGE): Locale Boundaries Technical Documentation'' published by the National Center for Education Statistics of the Department of Education. (b) Definitions.--In this section: (1) Covered entity.--The term ``covered entity'' means-- (A) a Federal, Tribal, State, or municipal agency; (B) a nongovernmental organization; (C) a community group; and (D) an academic institution. (2) Director.--The term ``Director'' means the Secretary of the Interior, acting through the Director of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service. (3) Eligible entity.--The term ``eligible entity'' means-- (A) a Tribal, State, or municipal agency; (B) a nongovernmental organization; (C) a community group; and (D) an academic institution. (4) Foundation.--The term ``Foundation'' means the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation established by section 2(a) of the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation Establishment Act (16 U.S.C. 3701(a)). (5) Program.--The term ``Program'' means the Urban Bird Treaty Program established under subsection (a)(1). (6) Urban.--The term ``urban'' has the meaning given the term ``urban area'' in section 101(a) of title 23, United States Code. (c) Authorization of Appropriations.--There is authorized to be appropriated to the Director to carry out this section $200,000 for each of fiscal years 2027 through 2033. Passed the House of Representatives September 14, 2026. Attest: Clerk. 119th CONGRESS 2d Session H. This bill honors former Representa-
tive Barbara Cubin, Wyoming’s first 
woman elected to Federal office. Dur-
ing her 14 years in Congress, Rep-
resentative Cubin strongly advocated 
for Wyoming and the West. As a found-
ing member of the Congressional West-
ern Caucus and chair of the House 
Committee on Natural Resources Sub-
committee on Energy and Mineral Re-
sources, she worked to advance respon-
sible development of America’s natural 
resources and improve the manage-
ment of our Federal lands. 
Representative Cubin also played an 
important role in shaping and telling 
the history of the American West. In 
1998, her legislation authorizing the 
National Historic Trails Interpretive 
Center in Casper was signed into law. 
The center is managed by the Bureau 
of Land Management, in partnership 
with local and private organizations, 
and offers free interactive exhibits and 
educational programming about Amer-
ica’s westward expansion. 
Unfortunately, last year, Representa-
tive Cubin publicly announced she had 
been diagnosed with Alzheimer’s dis-
ease. We continue to hold her, her fam-
ily, and all who know and love her in 
our prayers. 
It is a fitting tribute to her legacy 
that the center Representative Cubin 
helped establish will now bear her 
name. S. 790 recognizes her years of 
service to Wyoming and ensures that 
her contributions to the history and 
heritage of the American West are re-
membered for generations to come. 
I thank Representative H
AGEMAN and 
the entire Wyoming delegation for 
their leadership on this legislation and 
their commitment to honor Represent-
ative Cubin’s life and legacy.

support S. 790, and I reserve the bal-
ance of my time.

would redesignate the National His-

Former Representative Barbara 
Cubin was the first woman to represent 
Wyoming in Congress. Mr. Speaker, I 
am going to deviate from my notes

erated by the Bureau of Land Manage-

Mr. Speaker, I rise in support of H.R. 
3276, the Local Communities & Bird 
Habitat Stewardship Act of 2025. 
Birds are an important part of our 
Nation’s natural heritage and play an 
important role in healthy and resilient 
ecosystems. Millions of Americans also 
enjoy bird-watching each year, sup-
porting local economies and businesses 
across the country. Unfortunately, 
birds face several challenges in urban 
areas, including habitat loss and haz-
ards such as building collisions and 
light pollution. H.R. 3276 addresses 
these challenges by codifying the 
Urban Bird Treaty Program within the 
U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. 
The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service 
currently provides grants and technical 
assistance to communities and other 
eligible partners to conserve, restore, 
and enhance urban bird habitat, reduce 
hazards to birds, and engage the public 
in monitoring and conservation efforts. 
This legislation will enable this im-
portant work to continue with greater 
congressional oversight and account-
ability. 
Mr. Speaker, I just recently had the 
opportunity to visit Audubon, Arkan-
sas, and see the great work that they 
are doing with bird habitat and also to 
discuss again how healthy forests not 
only provide us with clean air and 
clean water, but they also provide ex-
cellent bird habitat. It is another rea-
son the Senate should pass the Fix Our 
Forests Act. 
Mr. Speaker, I reserve the balance of 
my time. 
Ms. ELFRETH. Mr. Speaker, I yield 
myself such time as I may consume. 
Mr. Speaker, H.R. 3276, the Local 
Communities & Bird Habitat Steward-
ship Act, would codify the U.S. Fish 
and Wildlife Service’s Urban Bird Trea-
ty Program and authorize annual fund-
ing through fiscal year 2033 to support 
local community investments in bird 
habitats across the country. 
Over the last 50 years, North America 
has lost nearly 3 billion breeding birds, 
a staggering 30 percent decline. While 
conservation is often seen as some-
thing that happens far out in the deep 
wilderness, nearly half of all migratory 
stopover hot spots in the U.S. fall with-
in metropolitan areas, making urban 
and suburban areas essential to bird 
conservation. 
Our built environments and back-
yards are essential mid-journey sanc-
tuaries for migratory birds, providing 
critical resting, feeding, and nesting 
grounds for migrating land birds. 
Since 1999, the Fish and Wildlife 
Service’s Urban Bird Treaty Program 
has supported voluntary, locally driven 
partnerships among municipal govern-
ments, tribes, nonprofits, and schools. 
These modest investments deliver out-
sized returns: restoring urban wet-
lands, controlling invasive species, re-
ducing hazards to birds like building 
glass and light pollution, and expand-
ing access to nature in underserved 
communities. 
Despite its overwhelming success, de-
mand for these grants far exceeds cur-
rent capacity. Without formal statu-
tory authority, the program relies on 
discretionary year-to-year funding, and 
as a result, the Fish and Wildlife Serv-
ice has been able to fulfill only about 
10 percent of the high-quality project 
applications it receives every year. 
H.R. 3276 would codify this program 
and authorize a competitive grant pro-
gram administered in partnership with 
the National Fish and Wildlife Founda-
tion. By passing this bill today, we are 
empowering local communities to lead 
on conservation, protect migratory 
birds, reduce hazards to birds, and con-
nect families to the outdoors. 
I applaud my colleague from Michi-
gan, Representative D
INGELL, for her 
leadership on this commonsense, lo-
cally-driven, bipartisan measure that 
protects biodiversity, strengthens local 
partnerships, and enriches our commu-
nities. 
Mr. Speaker, I urge all my colleagues 
to join me in support of her bill, and I 
reserve the balance of my time.
